task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The visible corpus is a single obfuscated bundle with no source map exposed; after obfuscation the anchor answer_function may remain a readable English identifier (renameGlobals:false), so the primary difficulty is semantic disambiguation among a small candidate set rather than recovering mangled names.
The target field name is assembled from fragments near the sink, so literal search does not reveal the anchor.
Browser capability samples are normalized, projected and transported through dynamic lanes before the digest is emitted.

The form-submit path crosses profile arming, consent gating, action routing, local event dispatch, route layers, asynchronous scheduling, tuple construction, runtime slot materialization, digest construction, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
Decoy modules emit bf-like shadow values and browser.preview objects that do not feed the requested browser_fingerprint field.
The target value is separated from the form submit by DOM CustomEvent, Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The final sink receives an already constructed browser_fingerprint value after projection and transport recovery.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is derived from navigator, screen, media/CSS support, canvas rendering and timezone signals. It is not a request signature, state encoding, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.
